newsitem.title: UK: BOE's George says UK investment banks can survive.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George says UK investment banks can survive.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Monday he expects that some of the few remaining British independent investment banks can survive.

Giving evidence before Parliament's Treasury select committee on the collapse of Barings, George said the fact that, since the collapse, some British merchant banks had come under foreign control was not mainly as a result of Barings.

"The only case that was a result of Barings was Barings itself," George said. "You have to distinguish the Barings effect. It may have accelerated the process, but the process was actually in the marketplace."

George noted that British investment bank S.G. Warburg, subsequently bought by Swiss Bank Corp, was already negotiating a sale when Barings collapsed, and that Deutsche Bank bought Morgan Grenfell as long ago as 1990.
The Governor said he did not see a 100 percent takeover of the current independent institutions.

"It's a perfectly reasonable business decision for people to take -- that they would thrive better, survive better with large parents than if they remained independednt," George said. "There will be room for both. There are some that are clearly intent on keeping independent and jolly good luck to them I say."
Barings was bought by Dutch financial services group Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING) after it collapsed.
Apart from Warburg, British investment bank Kleinwort Benson was bought by German bank Dresdner.
Those that remain independent include the quoted Schroders Plc and Hambros and the privately controlled Robert Fleming and N M Rothschild. All have trumpeted their intention to remain independent.
